doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Columbia engineers and three albums a year
summary: Fred Clough engineered many sessions under a Columbia contract requiring three albums a year for 17 years.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Were the first recordings that you made for Columbia in the studio without as many mics and so-on as they do now? I wasn’t around for those.
No, but we had great, famous engineers. Columbia had the time guys: Clough. Fred?
Fred Clough often did our sessions. We had to do three albums a year. That was my contract, and I never missed, that I can remember, in 17 years at Columbia.
I think you did more. I think if you – I look at the discography. I’ve done a count. You did at least three a year, sometimes more.
Then one for Fantasy [ ] we all decided. Many years – that would be four – then there’d be special products, where I had very little to do with it.
I remember I once went through your discography, and I did a count. It seemed every 12 to 14 weeks there would be a new Dave Brubeck recording on the market.
And Paul Desmond’s remark: “This group can make a recording for a streetcar token and a ham sandwich.”
